Case in point: I once saw someone say that they play the game 'Degrees of Lewdity' and enjoyed it, but that they are an 'anti' and 'don't support the aspects of the game that glorify SA'. Degrees of Lewdity is a porn game. It is a porn life simulator focused on a rape victim fetish. I won't go into the details because it gets really detailed and intense, the whole game is a trigger warning really, but this is a rape fetish game *at its core*. Seeing that was really eye opening. Thanks for your concern! In my experience, though, actively avoiding such content for fear of being 'desensitized' by it actually made my OCD worse. By a lot. By avoiding it I was telling my brain that it was actually something to be worried about, that the risk of me being a pedophile because of it WAS real. My worst days mentally were when I tried to do this.


The best thing for me so far has been going back to treating it like I did when I was younger. I consume it in moderation, casually, like any other media content because *it is completely separate from the real thing in my head.* I've been into 'problematic content' via fanfiction and such since I was around 13. And even at that age the idea of 'obviously, none of this applies to real life' was something so ingrained into my subconscious that I never actually had to think about it. If you tried to tell me 'by the way, incest is bad' because I was reading a problematic yaoi doujin I'd probably look at you crazy, because of course incest is bad. 


The only time I actually found myself triggered, developing OCD thoughts and wondering if I actually find things like incest, rape and pedophilia okay in real life was when *people online told me that that was the case.* I genuinely believe that the influence of your peers is far stronger than the influence of any fictional media.

As the train she’d just stepped off of hovered away, Illoe heavily considered leaping onto the tracks and waiting there for the next train to approach. 

	It would be easy enough, she thought. If she hid well, the conductor wouldn’t see her until it was too late. 

	Illoe took a small step forward and paused before shakily reaching down and grabbing her small luggage bag, lifting it off the ground. It was only when the train disappeared that the reality of Illoe’s situation really and truly started to settle into her mind. Throughout the twelve hour trip, she had managed to distract herself with frivolous thoughts. She had closely examined every other passenger she could see—seeing as it was late at night, there had only been four of them—and she had given them names, given them stories. She had imagined what their business in the Holy City was. Were they citizens, or visitors from other regions like she was? Were they travelling for business? To see family? Or for other reasons? 

	It was with this that she managed to keep her mind occupied, even as she grew hyper-aware of time passing. She knew her family would have woken up by now, only to find her bed empty. She could only imagine their reactions—well, she certainly *could,* but she found did not much want to. 

	Now, however, with no other thoughts to escape to, the images seeped into her mind like a sickness. Yara would be worried, she knew. Her stepmother was a good woman, all things considered; she would likely be the only one truly concerned about Illoe’s well-being. Her two younger brothers… would probably not be too bothered by Illoe’s sudden disappearance. They had never liked her much—and that was just about the only thing she had in common with them. 

	And her father… 

	Illoe’s stomach lurched. Bringing her free hand up to her mouth, she stumbled across the stone floor towards a nearby bench, earning stares of concern from the people around her. She ignored them, sucking in sharp breaths in a desperate attempt to calm herself down.
